title: Awarapan 2 Has Wrapped Shooting. Emraan Hashmi Is Bringing Shivam Back After Nineteen Years.
excerpt: Vishesh Films confirms the sequel has finished filming across Rajasthan and Southeast Asia. Disha Patani joins the franchise. August 14 is the date.
body:
Some characters refuse to die. Shivam from *Awarapan* was supposed to. The 2007 film ended with a dream sequence — Emraan Hashmi's bruised, morally compromised fixer reuniting with the woman he loved, played by Shriya Saran, in a moment that felt more like an afterlife than a future. Audiences understood that Shivam was gone. The film flopped at the box office. And then something unusual happened: it refused to go away.

Television reruns turned *Awarapan* into a cult film. "Toh Phir Aao" and "Tera Mera Rishta" became the kind of songs that entire generations associate with late-night FM radio and early YouTube. The character of Shivam — a man caught between loyalty to a gangster and love for a woman he could never have — became one of Emraan Hashmi's most enduring screen identities. Fans have been asking for a sequel for nearly two decades.

On Thursday, Vishesh Films announced that the wait is nearly over. Principal photography on *Awarapan 2* has wrapped. The film was shot across Rajasthan and Southeast Asia, and is set for a worldwide theatrical release on August 14, 2026 — India's Independence Day, a date that signals serious commercial ambitions.

## Shivam Returns, the World Expands

The sequel picks up from those final dream-like moments of the original. Shivam comes back to life and crosses paths with a new character played by Disha Patani, who enters the Vishesh Films universe for the first time. It is a continuation, not a reboot — a distinction that matters for a franchise whose emotional weight rests entirely on character history.

Nitin Kakkar directs, stepping in for Mohit Suri, who helmed the original. Bilal Siddiqui has written the screenplay. Vishesh Bhatt produces under the Vishesh Films banner, keeping the project within the family ecosystem that built the first film.

"Awarapan is an emotion so large that it's meant for the big screen," Bhatt said in a statement accompanying the wrap announcement. "It also presents exotic settings and large-scale sequences, but fundamentally it's built on our core principles of layered storytelling with powerful characters and rich music. Emraan felt the angst of Shivam so deeply that he stepped into character in a heartbeat."

## What the Diaspora Remembers

For NRIs who grew up in the mid-2000s, *Awarapan* occupies a specific emotional register. It was the film you watched on Zee Cinema during college breaks, the one whose songs played on loop during long drives. The melancholy of Shivam's impossible love story — trapped between duty to a violent boss and feelings for a woman he was supposed to keep captive — resonated with audiences who rarely saw Bollywood explore moral ambiguity with that kind of sincerity.

The original was not a commercial success. It earned roughly ₹18 crore against a modest budget. But in the years that followed, it accumulated something that no box office number can measure: genuine affection. When Vishesh Films posted the wrap photo on Instagram — Emraan holding the clapboard — the caption read: "OGs know this isn't just a wrap. He came back for you."

## The Music Question

One of the biggest expectations surrounding the sequel is the soundtrack. The original *Awarapan* album, composed by Pritam and featuring vocals by Mustafa Zahid of Roxen, is still streamed millions of times monthly. Sony Music India continues as the music partner for the sequel, and Vishesh Bhatt has indicated that multiple composers are working on the album. For a franchise where the music is arguably more remembered than the plot, this is where the sequel will be judged most harshly.

## The Landscape for August 14

An Independence Day release puts *Awarapan 2* in a high-stakes corridor. The holiday window typically attracts multiple big-ticket releases, and Emraan Hashmi's recent box office track record has been mixed. But *Awarapan 2* has something that most sequels do not: a character that audiences genuinely want to see again. Whether that translates to opening-weekend numbers will depend on trailers, music, and early word of mouth. The shooting is done. The wait now begins in earnest.
